_meta.modeledAfter: Strong mid-size regional cinema camera rental house (Camtec/Koerner/Rule/CineMechanics/PC&E tier)
_meta.caveat: Category taxonomy, product mix, and day rates are benchmarked against real published rates. Serials, barcodes, purchase dates, condition grades, bin locations, utilization, and revenue are SYNTHETIC — realistic distributions, not real records from any house.
_meta.schemaNote: www/src/lib/db/schema.ts has no asset/inventory layer today — package_items.gear_id points at a product catalog row, not a physical unit. This file is a reference for what a future asset-tracking layer would need, not something the current schema can fully absorb. See rental_house_inventory table for the thin slice that DOES map today (day_rate/week_rate/quantity_on_hand per product).

As-Of Date.why: Valuation and aging date. Drives asset age, book value and service-due status.

Fiscal Year Start.why: Start of the YTD utilization window.

Days in YTD Window.why: Calendar days from FY start through the as-of date.

3-Day Week Multiplier.why: Standard film/TV convention: a 3-day week bills at 3x the day rate.

Weekly (7-Day) Multiplier.why: 7-day pickup-to-return week. Houses land between 3x and 4x; 4x is typical for a full week.

Monthly Multiplier.why: Monthly is ~10-12x daily, not 30x. Roughly 3x the weekly.

Weekend Rate Multiplier.why: Thu/Fri PM pickup to Mon AM return bills as a single day. Near-universal convention.

Damage Waiver %.why: Charged on top of the rental rate; caps renter liability at 25% of replacement value.

Typical Deal-Memo Discount off Card.why: Real negotiated rate vs. published list on a multi-day booking. Card rate is an opening position.

Sub-Rental Cost as % of Day Rate.why: What the house pays a peer house when it sub-rents an item in.

Target Time Utilization.why: Camera rental runs structurally below the 60-70% general-equipment benchmark. A flagship body doing 45% of days is a star.

Utilization Floor (flag below).why: Assets under this are candidates for sale, repositioning or rate cuts.

Service Due Warning Window (days).why: Assets due for service inside this window flag as DUE SOON.

Insurance Rate (% of repl. value/yr).why: Annual inland marine premium as a share of insured replacement value.

Residual Value at End of Life.why: Secondary-market exit value. Camera gear typically clears 10-20% of original cost.

departmentSummary.Department: •  Camera rental does not hit the 60-70% utilization benchmark quoted for general equipment rental. A flagship body working 45% of available
•     days is a star performer; 20-30% is normal, because most bookings are one to three days with prep and turnaround on either side.
•  Read the two revenue-quality metrics as a pair. Rate realization is what you collect versus list on the days an item actually goes out.
•     Dollar utilization is revenue versus billing every unit at list on every available day - a ceiling nobody reaches, useful only as a trend.
•  Rate realization is not one number. A camera body holds ~40% of card because the body rate survives negotiation. Grip and media hold 10-13%
•     because they ride inside a truck package or a body package and collect a fraction of their piece rate. That spread is the real pricing story.
•  Grip and expendables carry the line-item count; cameras and lenses carry the dollars. Optimizing one does not optimize the other.
•  Cheap high-turn gear returns more than 1x its replacement value a year. A $230 C-stand out 150 days at even $2 net beats a $95,000 body on
•     return-on-asset - which is exactly why houses keep buying grip and agonize over every camera purchase.
•  Camera bodies lose 30-40% of value in year one and reach end of competitive rental life at 24-36 months. Lenses run 48-60 months.
•  Payback at list is a fiction check, not a plan: real payback runs 2-4x longer once discount, downtime, service and insurance come out.
•  20-35% of a typical job's line items get sub-rented from a peer or national house. That is normal practice, not a coverage failure.
